scams.name: Illegal Cross-Border Taxi Racket (JB ↔ Singapore via Sultan Iskandar CIQ)
scams.description: The JB–Singapore illegal cross-border taxi trade is Johor Bahru's most-enforced 2025 transport scam and the single highest-risk shortcut Singaporean day-trippers take. Unlicensed drivers solicit inside the Bangunan Sultan Iskandar CIQ, at JB Sentral, outside City Square, and via closed WhatsApp/Telegram groups, undercutting the legitimate cross-border taxi stand by quoting RM 40–RM 80 flat to Woodlands or RM 120 onwards to central Singapore. The vehicles are uninsured, often Singapore-registered MPVs without Vehicle Entry Permits, and passengers share full criminal exposure. 2025 community reports document a Malaysian operator jailed after taking up to RM 3,300 daily from touting. A 2024 community report details the worst-case anchor: a girl allegedly kidnapped in Malaysia after using an illegal cross-border ride. Additional community reports document the baseline and the JPJ/LTA crackdown context. The 2025 scam pattern: (a) a friendly 'driver' messages you on a public WhatsApp group or approaches at CIQ offering 'direct to Orchard, no queue, RM 80'; (b) on Singapore side, LTA enforcement has fined passengers up to SGD 3,000 and issued six-month jail notices under the Road Traffic Act; (c) JPJ Johor seized four Singapore-registered vehicles used for illegal rides in a single September 2025 operation (Malay Mail); (d) some 'rides' are actually abduction bait — the 2024 Malaysia kidnap case involved a woman who boarded through Telegram; (e) drivers coach passengers to lie at immigration ('say we are friends') — which criminalises YOU, not just the driver; (f) no insurance coverage whatsoever — accident victims have been left with five-figure hospital bills. For travelers: (1) use ONLY the licensed cross-border taxi stand at JB Sentral or Ban San Street Terminal (Queen Street, Singapore) — flat fare roughly RM 80 / SGD 50 for a 4-seat car; (2) the public bus (CW1/CW2/CW5/SBS 170) crosses the Causeway for SGD 3–SGD 5 and is the safest budget option; (3) KTM Shuttle Tebrau train Woodlands↔JB Sentral is SGD 5 and takes 5 minutes across; (4) NEVER use Telegram/WhatsApp 'cross-border' groups — every major 2025 arrest came from those channels; (5) Grab/Maxim work WITHIN Malaysia only — a Grab cannot legally cross into Singapore, and a Singapore Grab cannot legally enter Malaysia; (6) if a driver tells you to 'say we are friends at immigration', walk away — you are about to commit a Customs offence; (7) verify any cross-border taxi licence sticker (pink 'cross-border' plate in Malaysia, yellow 'Teksi 4PV' in JB) before boarding; (8) LTA Singapore tip-off hotline 1800 CALL LTA (1800 2255 582) for reporting; PDRM Johor 07-221 2999.
scams.avoidance: Use ONLY licensed cross-border taxis at JB Sentral or Ban San Street (Queen St, SG) — RM 80 / SGD 50 flat Public bus (CW1/CW2/170) SGD 3–SGD 5 OR KTM Shuttle Tebrau SGD 5 / 5 min NEVER book via WhatsApp/Telegram 'cross-border' groups — LTA fines passengers up to SGD 3,000 Grab/Maxim do NOT cross the border — refuse any 'Grab-like' cross-border offer Walk away if driver says 'tell immigration we are friends'
scams.location: Bangunan Sultan Iskandar CIQ arrivals/departures, JB Sentral taxi queues, Woodlands Checkpoint Singapore side, Ban San Street cross-border terminal, Telegram/WhatsApp 'JB-SG ride' groups, City Square Mall pickup zone

scams.name: Counterfeit Luxury-Goods Confidence Trick (Pasar Karat, Holiday Plaza, Jalan Wong Ah Fook)
scams.description: Johor Bahru operates one of Southeast Asia's most prolific counterfeit-luxury-goods ecosystems, anchored around Pasar Karat (Jalan Segget night flea market), Holiday Plaza, and older shoplots along Jalan Wong Ah Fook and Jalan Dhoby. The December 2024 Johor police raid — Free Malaysia Today and NST reported RM 1.4 million in fake branded goods seized from a single JB syndicate — is the single biggest enforcement anchor of this scam. 2025 community reports document the 'Grade AAA' tier-pricing culture, with earlier community threads naming JB as the regional hub. Additional community reports document the cross-border fraud overlap where counterfeit 'pre-loved' Chanel/LV are resold to Singaporeans. The 2025 scam pattern: (a) a shop in Holiday Plaza or KSL basement quotes a Gucci Marmont bag at RM 350 instead of the authentic RM 5,000, claiming 'factory overrun from the Vietnam plant'; (b) 'Grade AAA mirror quality' or 'unauthorised authentic' lexicon is a dead giveaway — there is no such legal category; (c) carrying counterfeits into Singapore triggers SGD 10,000 fines and 3-year jail under the Copyright Act (Singapore Customs seized over 4,000 fake items from JB day-trippers in 2024–2025); (d) cash-only, no receipts, 'the Jimmy Choo box is separate RM 30' pricing tactics; (e) follow-on WhatsApp upsell — after your first purchase, the seller adds you to a Telegram group for 'VIP drops'; (f) fake Rolex sellers at Jalan Dhoby night stalls quoting RM 800–RM 1,500 for 'Super Clone 904L' watches that fail within 90 days. For travelers: (1) assume anything 'designer' under 30% of retail in JB is counterfeit — there is no legitimate outlet discount that deep; (2) for genuine discounts on authentic goods, use Johor Premium Outlets (Indahpura) — Coach, Michael Kors, Tumi run 30–60% off RRP with authenticity cards; (3) NEVER cross back into Singapore with counterfeit goods — ICA routinely seizes at Woodlands and Tuas; declare nothing dutiable; (4) if you're buying for yourself knowing it's fake, understand Malaysia's Trade Descriptions Act 2011 can fine buyers RM 250,000 and seize goods at the JB side; (5) inspect stitching, hardware engravings, serial-number tags, and lining seams — authentic Chanel/LV have serial numbers inside a hidden pocket; (6) avoid 'tour guide' or 'shopping buddy' offers at CIQ — they earn commission from counterfeit shops, not from you; (7) KPDN Johor hotline 07-224 3455 for reporting; PDRM commercial crime +603-2610 1559.
scams.avoidance: Assume 'designer' under 30% of retail = counterfeit — no legitimate JB outlet goes deeper For genuine deals, use Johor Premium Outlets (Indahpura) — Coach/MK/Tumi 30–60% off with authenticity cards NEVER cross into Singapore with fakes — SGD 10,000 fine, 3-year jail under Copyright Act Inspect stitching, hardware engravings, serial tags; refuse 'tour guide/shopping buddy' commission offers KPDN Johor 07-224 3455 for reporting
scams.location: Pasar Karat (Jalan Segget night flea market), Holiday Plaza, Jalan Wong Ah Fook shophouses, Jalan Dhoby night stalls, KSL City Mall basement lots, Komtar JBCC knockoff corners

scams.name: Motorbike Snatch-Theft on Jalan Wong Ah Fook, Taman Pelangi & Kampung Melayu Majidee
scams.description: Motorcycle 'ragut' (snatch-theft) is Johor Bahru's most physically dangerous 2025 street crime and the leading cause of tourist A&E visits at Hospital Sultanah Aminah. Two riders on a kapcai motorcycle pull alongside a pedestrian, the pillion yanks phone or bag in a single pass at 40 km/h, and they disappear into the Jalan Tebrau traffic grid within 90 seconds. Victims are commonly dragged — fractured wrists, dislocated shoulders, concussions from hitting the kerb. Community reports document a Singaporean victim losing documents plus cash on Jalan Wong Ah Fook, and 2025 community threads name JB among the highest-risk Malaysian cities for snatch-theft. The 2025 pattern: (a) pillion rider targets visibly-tourist pedestrians walking on the kerb side with phones in hand; (b) sunset-to-midnight Jalan Wong Ah Fook between City Square and JB Sentral is the densest hotspot, followed by Taman Pelangi bar strip, Kampung Melayu Majidee, and Jalan Tun Abdul Razak; (c) handbags worn on the road-facing shoulder are torn off — elderly victims have been pulled into the road; (d) phone-snatch rate has spiked with smartphone resale value — iPhone 15 Pro Max refences sell for RM 3,000 on Telegram fence markets; (e) a new 2025 variant: rider pretends to be a lost rider asking directions while the pillion unzips your bag; (f) Pasir Gudang and Larkin Sentral bus terminal approaches are secondary hotspots for departing tourists. For travelers: (1) carry nothing on your road-facing shoulder — swap your crossbody strap to the building side EVERY time you cross a street; (2) never use your phone while walking within 3 metres of a kerb — step fully into a shop, mall, or café to check Google Maps; (3) after sunset, prefer Grab/Maxim (RM 6–RM 15 for short hops) over walking — especially between JB Sentral and KSL/Mid Valley Southkey; (4) use a zipped anti-theft crossbody worn diagonally across the chest; never a backpack with unzipped outer pocket; (5) walk facing oncoming traffic so you see approaching bikes; (6) if snatched, do NOT hold on — elderly victims have been dragged 20+ metres with fractured wrists; (7) PDRM emergency 999; Tourist Police JB 07-222 2999; Hospital Sultanah Aminah 07-223 1666; (8) report to file a police report within 24 hours for travel-insurance claims and ICA re-entry documentation.
scams.avoidance: Swap crossbody strap to building-side EVERY street crossing — never road-facing shoulder NEVER phone-in-hand while walking near traffic — step fully into a shop first After sunset, use Grab/Maxim (RM 6–RM 15) not walking — especially JB Sentral ↔ KSL Zipped anti-theft crossbody, not backpack; walk facing oncoming traffic If snatched, LET GO — elderly victims dragged 20+ metres PDRM 999; Tourist Police JB 07-222 2999
scams.location: Jalan Wong Ah Fook (JB Sentral to City Square strip), Taman Pelangi bar/restaurant area, Kampung Melayu Majidee, Jalan Tun Abdul Razak, Larkin Sentral bus terminal approaches, Pasir Gudang light-industrial zone edges

scams.name: Fake Parking-Fine QR-Code Scam (bogus MBJB SPOT phishing slips)
scams.description: Johor Bahru's fake-parking-fine phishing slip is one of 2025's fastest-growing documented scams against Singaporean self-drive day-trippers and KL weekenders. Scammers print authentic-looking Majlis Bandaraya Johor Bahru (MBJB) 'saman' notices with a prominent QR code and slip them under the windshield wipers of Singapore-plated and rental cars parked on Jalan Ibrahim, Jalan Tan Hiok Nee, the Jalan Dhoby heritage strip, KSL City Mall street parking, and around Mount Austin eateries. Scanning the QR opens a spoofed MBJB page or a phishing banking login, and typed-in credentials drain accounts within hours — one Malaysian man reported losing RM 3,000 in a single compromised session per KPDN advisories. 2025 community reports document the pattern, with earlier community reports documenting the earlier fake-parking-ticket wave, and cross-border-tourist reports showing the same crews also spoof PDRM SMS. The 2025 pattern: (a) a crisp-printed 'saman' slip with MBJB logo, a fake reference number, and a QR code appears under your wiper within 30–60 minutes of you parking; (b) QR scans to a fake 'jompay' or 'Touch 'n Go' page OR to a spoofed FPX banking login; (c) entered credentials are used within minutes to drain accounts and enrol the phone for device-transfer; (d) 2025 escalation: 'saman' slips now include a WhatsApp number claiming to be an 'officer' who coaches you through the 'payment' live; (e) Singapore-plated cars targeted at Jalan Dhoby heritage zone, Mount Austin hawker centres, and KSL overflow lots — drivers desperate to clear fees before ferry-back timing; (f) genuine MBJB 'kompaun' are paid ONLY via the official MBJB SPOT app or at the MBJB counter (Wisma MBJB, Jalan Dato Onn) — never via a QR on paper. For travelers: (1) NEVER scan a QR on a physical parking slip — MBJB, DBKL, and every Malaysian municipal council issues digital-first e-summons via their app, not printed QR; (2) download the official 'MBJB SPOT' app on arrival (iOS App Store / Google Play, publisher 'Majlis Bandaraya Johor Bahru') — any legitimate saman appears in the app tied to your plate; (3) if you receive a physical slip, photograph it, DO NOT pay, and check the MBJB SPOT app OR call MBJB 07-222 6222 during office hours (Mon–Fri 8 AM–5 PM); (4) pay for street parking via the MBJB SPOT app or Touch 'n Go eWallet pre-purchase — NEVER via a QR on a posted sign you can't verify; (5) prefer paid indoor mall car parks (City Square RM 4/hour, KSL RM 2/hour, Komtar JBCC RM 3/hour) — they use automated ticketing and cannot be spoofed; (6) if your phone was compromised, call your bank IMMEDIATELY to freeze, and file a PDRM report at the nearest balai within 24 hours for chargeback evidence; (7) CCID Cyber Crime Scamenquiries hotline 013-211 1222 or ccid.rmp.gov.my; (8) save Tourist Police JB 07-222 2999.
scams.avoidance: NEVER scan a QR on a physical parking slip — MBJB issues ALL saman via the MBJB SPOT app only Download 'MBJB SPOT' on arrival (publisher: Majlis Bandaraya Johor Bahru) — real fines appear tied to your plate Prefer indoor mall parking (City Square, KSL, Komtar JBCC) — automated ticketing can't be spoofed Verify suspicious slips via MBJB 07-222 6222 or the app — NEVER call WhatsApp numbers on the slip CCID Cyber Crime 013-211 1222
scams.location: Jalan Ibrahim street parking, Jalan Tan Hiok Nee heritage strip, Jalan Dhoby pedestrian zone edges, KSL City Mall overflow street bays, Mount Austin hawker-centre streets, Taman Molek cafés, Puteri Harbour waterfront lots

scams.name: Fake-Banknote Change Scam at Pasar Malam, Ramadan Bazaars & Hawker Stalls
scams.description: Counterfeit ringgit notes — especially the redesigned RM 50 and RM 20 series — circulate heavily through Johor Bahru's night markets, Ramadan bazaars, and hawker stalls, where a Singaporean visitor spending SGD 50 / RM 170 becomes a prime target for fake-change substitution. Transactions are cash, fast, poorly-lit, and conducted against a wall of queueing buyers — the perfect environment for a vendor to shuffle a fake RM 20 or RM 50 into your change stack. Bank Negara Malaysia security-features reference (BNM.gov.my) lists the watermark, security thread, and holographic latent image that genuine notes carry. 2025 community reports document the overlap ecosystem where R&F Mall / City Square beggars use counterfeit notes to launder small bills. Community reports also document the broader counterfeit-money enforcement context, SGD cross-border exchange risk, and syndicate overlap. The 2025 pattern: (a) you pay for RM 6 nasi lemak with a fresh RM 50 from a Singapore money changer; vendor makes change from a thick stack in a waist-pouch and slides you RM 40 back, one RM 20 note of which is a passable counterfeit; (b) counterfeit RM 50 notes from an active Johor-origin syndicate — Johor police seized over RM 400,000 in fake banknotes in 2024–2025 (The Star); (c) short-change variant at Jalan Dhoby night stalls — vendor deliberately 'miscounts' and pockets RM 10; (d) 'no change' pressure — a RM 4 drink 'costs' RM 5 because the vendor claims zero coins available; (e) cross-border money-changer short-change at Sultan Iskandar CIQ — smaller booths within Bangunan Sultan Iskandar short SGD 5–SGD 20 on RM 500 conversions and rely on time-pressured travellers not recounting; (f) Ramadan bazaar 2025 surge — every Ramadan (Feb–Mar 2026) sees a spike in both counterfeit-change and short-change reports per Bernama. For travelers: (1) use Touch 'n Go eWallet, GrabPay, Boost, or DuitNow QR at EVERY hawker stall, bazaar, and street vendor — cashless is counterfeit-proof and 90% of JB vendors accept it in 2026; (2) if you must pay cash, use exact-change SMALL notes (RM 1, RM 5, RM 10) — never hand over a RM 50 or RM 100 at a hawker stall; (3) exchange currency ONLY at licensed money changers INSIDE major malls (Mid Valley Southkey, City Square 'The Money Changer' branded counter, KSL basement) — avoid kiosk stalls at CIQ; (4) count change IN FRONT of the vendor, under good light, before putting your wallet away; (5) check RM 50/RM 100 watermark by tilting — genuine notes show a raised hibiscus and colour-shift on the silver strip; (6) keep daily cash under RM 200 — hotel safe the rest; (7) if you receive counterfeit, file at nearest PDRM balai (Balai Polis Tampoi or Balai Polis Johor Bahru Selatan) — bank tellers will NOT accept counterfeit for deposit; (8) compare money-changer rates on ringgittotheworld.com or XE before handing over cash.
scams.avoidance: Use Touch 'n Go / GrabPay / DuitNow QR at EVERY hawker stall — 90% of JB vendors accept cashless in 2026 If paying cash, use exact-change small notes (RM 1/RM 5/RM 10) — never hand over RM 50/RM 100 at a stall Exchange ONLY at mall money changers (Mid Valley Southkey, City Square, KSL) — not CIQ kiosks Count change IN FRONT of vendor under good light; tilt RM 50/RM 100 to check watermark + colour-shift Keep daily cash under RM 200
scams.location: Jalan Dhoby pasar malam, Ramadan bazaars (Taman Pelangi, Taman Molek, Larkin), hawker stalls along Jalan Wong Ah Fook, Bangunan Sultan Iskandar CIQ money-changer kiosks, R&F Mall food-court stalls

scams.name: Budget-Massage Upsell & Cupping-Blister Scam (Jalan Dhoby, Taman Pelangi, KSL area)
scams.description: Johor Bahru's cheap massage ecosystem — shopfronts advertising RM 38 full-body and RM 48 foot-reflexology — is the single most-reported overcharging scam against Singaporean day-trippers and KL weekenders in 2025. The business model is bait-and-upsell: the advertised RM 38 rate is real but the therapist starts adding 'treatments' halfway through, and a non-English-speaking customer finds themselves facing a RM 300–RM 600 bill at checkout and, in the worst documented case, second-degree burns from aggressive cupping (fire cupping, 'bekam') performed by untrained staff. Community reports document a Singaporean requiring medical treatment costing nearly SGD 800 after a JB fire-cupping session at a budget shopfront. Additional community reports document the sexual-misconduct overlap in the same shop tier and the privacy-violation concerns (hidden CCTV in a KSL massage room). Community-baseline threads name massage-upsell as a top-3 avoidance topic for Singaporeans crossing to JB. The 2025 pattern: (a) a shopfront on Jalan Dhoby, Taman Pelangi, or around KSL advertises 'Full Body RM 38 / 60min' — the rate is genuine but lures you in; (b) 10 minutes into the massage the therapist starts offering 'tambah' (add-ons): hot stone RM 60, ginger wrap RM 50, traditional cupping RM 80, 'special herbal oil' RM 40; (c) English-limited customers nod to everything, and checkout is RM 300–RM 600; (d) cupping burn risk — untrained staff use open-flame fire cupping with glass cups, leaving second-degree blisters and infection risk requiring JB hospital treatment; (e) 'happy ending' illegal upsell in the sexual-misconduct tier — never a feature of legitimate spas and a hard indicator you are in an unlicensed venue; (f) illegal in-room recording per the 2023 KSL CCTV case; (g) payment only in cash 'because terminal broken' and refusal to provide an itemized receipt. For travelers: (1) use ONLY KPDN-licensed spas with posted itemized price boards at the entrance and online reviews 4.3+ on Google (e.g., Thai Odyssey at KSL/Mid Valley Southkey, Urban Retreat at City Square, Nexus Well-Being); (2) CONFIRM the total price in writing BEFORE you lie down — take a photo of the price list with your phone; (3) refuse every 'tambah' upsell mid-session — 'tidak, terima kasih' ('no, thank you') and do not negotiate; (4) NEVER accept fire cupping from any unlicensed staff — it requires a registered traditional-medicine practitioner (TCM); (5) pay by card or Touch 'n Go eWallet — demand an itemized receipt; card means chargeback is possible; (6) women traveling solo: prefer female-therapist-only spas inside mall venues (Mid Valley Southkey, Toppen Shopping Centre) — avoid standalone shopfronts; (7) if pressured or touched inappropriately, LEAVE immediately — pay NOTHING, and report to PDRM Tourist Police 07-222 2999; (8) cupping-burn injuries: Hospital Sultanah Aminah ER 07-223 1666 or KPJ Johor Specialist 07-225 3000 — document with photos for travel insurance.
scams.avoidance: Use ONLY KPDN-licensed mall spas (Thai Odyssey KSL, Urban Retreat City Square, Nexus Well-Being) — 4.3+ Google reviews CONFIRM total price in writing + photograph the price board BEFORE lying down Refuse every 'tambah' upsell — 'tidak, terima kasih' — no negotiation NEVER accept fire cupping from unlicensed staff — requires registered TCM practitioner Pay by card or Touch 'n Go for chargeback protection; PDRM Tourist Police JB 07-222 2999
scams.location: Jalan Dhoby budget massage shopfronts, Taman Pelangi standalone massage parlours, KSL City Mall unlicensed upper-floor parlours, JB Sentral adjacent shopfronts, Jalan Wong Ah Fook back-alley parlours
